title: Etale locus of a group homomorphism is translation invariant
statement: Let A be a nonzero abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety] over a field k, let H be a group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] over k, and let f:A\to H be a homomorphism. For every k-point a of A, translation by a carries the etale locus of f isomorphically to itself. Consequently the etale locus is empty or all of A, and f is etale if and only if it is etale at the identity.

source.place: Groupoid Schemes, lemma on etaleness of multiplication by d, proof using translations

proof.text: For a k-point a of A, the left translation L_a on A and the left translation L_{f(a)} on H are isomorphisms, with inverses given by translation by a^{-1} and f(a)^{-1}, by [lem-sc-translation-automorphism]. The homomorphism identity gives L_{f(a)}\circ f=f\circ L_a. Since isomorphisms are etale and etaleness is stable under composition, this commuting square transports pointwise etaleness between x and a\cdot x; this is the elementary composition argument (f=L_{f(a)}^{-1}\circ f\circ L_a).

source.place: ## Proof, step 1 (translation invariance of the etale locus)

proof.text: For any point x of A, extend its residue field κ(x) to an algebraic closure K and choose a point x_K of A_K above x. By [lem-sc-etale-base-change-geometric], f is etale at x if and only if f_K is etale at x_K. The point x_K is a K-point, so translation by x_K^{-1} is an isomorphism carrying x_K to the identity; the composition argument of step 1 shows that f_K is etale at x_K if and only if it is etale at the identity. Applying the same base-change equivalence to the identity gives that f is etale at x if and only if it is etale at the identity. Hence the etale locus is empty or all of A, and f is etale exactly when it is etale at the identity.
